newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Hashimoto will make Asian trip.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Hashimoto will make Asian trip.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Tuesday he would go ahead with a five-nation Asian tour next week despite the Lima hostage crisis.
The nine-day trip, starting on January 7, will take Hashimoto to Brunei, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Vietnam.

Earlier this week, at the height of the Lima hostage siege, foreign ministry officials said Hashimoto was considering cancelling the trip because of the siege at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
A government source said Hashimoto believed the hostage crisis was being well handled and it would be "inexcusable to allow such an important diplomatic schedule to be swayed by guerrillas".
"I am going ahead with the trip," Hashimoto told reporters. "I place my entire trust in Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori and have made arrangements so I can always be contacted."
Hashimoto's decision appeared to be a new sign that the siege might be near an end.
In Lima on Monday, Peruvian Prime Minister Alberto Pandolfi said he expected the siege to end with all 83 remaining hostages released unharmed by their Marxist captors.
"We are sure that the continuing sound handling of the situation will allow a solution that protects the physical well-being and lives of all of the hostages," Pandolfi said in a speech.
The prime minister's statement reflected a new mood of hope since the first face-to-face meeting on Saturday between the guerrillas in the residence and government negotiator Domingo Palermo.
About 20 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels took over the Japan ambassador's residence on December 17, seizing more than 500 hostages. Only 83 remain.
Last week, Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda cancelled a visit to South Korea because of the crisis.
